# xrdbi

xrdbi is a [DBI](https://dbi.r-dbi.org) backend for
[xarray](https://xarray.dev). The “database” is an xarray Dataset in a
live Python session, reached through
[reticulate](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/), and a connection is
a handle to it:

- tables are the Dataset’s variables
- fields are a variable’s dimensions and coordinates, then the variable
  itself
- a statement is a Python expression over `ds`, and its result arrives
  as tidy rows, one per cell

dplyr verbs compile to the same statements,
[`xr_raster()`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/xr_raster.md)
renders a slab as a raster, and
[`xr_chunks()`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/xr_chunks.md)
maps the storage chunks a selection touches. Anything xarray can open is
in reach: netCDF and HDF5 files, zarr in the cloud, virtual and icechunk
stores, and, through the gdalxarray engine, anything GDAL reads.

Documentation: <https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/>

## Installation

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("mdsumner/xrdbi")
```

xrdbi declares its core Python requirements, xarray and netCDF4, when it
loads, so with no Python configured, reticulate provisions them on first
use. Other engines and file systems are declared the same way, as in the
example below. To use your own Python, conda or pixi, or the
gdal-r-python image, see [Python
environments](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/articles/python-environments.html).

## Example

The ARCO ERA5 reanalysis on Google Cloud is one zarr store: 273
variables, hourly on a quarter-degree global grid.

``` r
library(DBI)
library(xrdbi)
reticulate::py_require(c("zarr", "gcsfs"))

era <- "gs://gcp-public-data-arco-era5/ar/full_37-1h-0p25deg-chunk-1.zarr-v3"
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), era, engine = "zarr",
                 storage_options = reticulate::dict(token = "anon"))
con
#> <XarrayConnection>
#>   dsn: gs://gcp-public-data-arco-era5/ar/full_37-1h-0p25deg-chunk-1.zarr-v3
#>   dims: time: 1323648, latitude: 721, longitude: 1440, level: 37
#>   vars: 100m_u_component_of_wind, 100m_v_component_of_wind, ... (273 total)
dbListFields(con, "2m_temperature")
#> [1] "time"           "latitude"       "longitude"      "2m_temperature"
```

A statement is xarray’s own selection language. One value, near Hobart:

``` r
dbGetQuery(con,
  "ds['2m_temperature'].sel(time='2020-01-01T00', latitude=-42.75, longitude=147.25)")
#>   latitude longitude       time 2m_temperature
#> 1   -42.75    147.25 2020-01-01       290.9427
```

dplyr filters compile to a selection, oriented to each coordinate’s
direction (latitude here runs north to south), and
[`show_query()`](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/explain.html)
prints the statement:

``` r
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
tas <- tbl(con, "2m_temperature") |>
  filter(time == as.POSIXct("2020-01-01 00:00", tz = "UTC"),
         latitude > -43.5, latitude < -42, longitude > 146.5, longitude < 148)
show_query(tas)
#> ds['2m_temperature'].sel(latitude=slice(-42, -43.5), longitude=slice(146.5, 148), time='2020-01-01T00:00:00').pipe(lambda a: a.isel(latitude=(a['latitude'].to_index() > -43.5) & (a['latitude'].to_index() < -42), longitude=(a['longitude'].to_index() > 146.5) & (a['longitude'].to_index() < 148)))
collect(tas)
#> # A tibble: 25 × 4
#>    latitude longitude time                `2m_temperature`
#>       <dbl>     <dbl> <dttm>                         <dbl>
#>  1   -42.25    146.75 2020-01-01 00:00:00          287.470
#>  2   -42.25    147    2020-01-01 00:00:00          288.478
#>  3   -42.25    147.25 2020-01-01 00:00:00          290.044
#>  4   -42.25    147.5  2020-01-01 00:00:00          291.181
#>  5   -42.25    147.75 2020-01-01 00:00:00          292.700
#>  6   -42.5     146.75 2020-01-01 00:00:00          287.864
#>  7   -42.5     147    2020-01-01 00:00:00          289.038
#>  8   -42.5     147.25 2020-01-01 00:00:00          290.086
#>  9   -42.5     147.5  2020-01-01 00:00:00          291.287
#> 10   -42.5     147.75 2020-01-01 00:00:00          292.118
#> # ℹ 15 more rows
```

Every read is sized before it happens, and refused above a limit:

``` r
try(dbReadTable(con, "2m_temperature"))
#> Error : materializing 1,374,264,299,520 cells exceeds the guard (10,000,000); subset first, raise options(xrdbi.max_cells=), or use force = TRUE
```

One hour of the whole globe is one stored chunk, and
[`xr_raster()`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/xr_raster.md)
renders it as a raster with its georeferencing, ready for gdalraster:

``` r
r <- xr_raster(con, "ds['2m_temperature'].sel(time='2020-01-01T00')")
temps <- function(x) rgb(colorRamp(hcl.colors(11, "Temps"))(x), maxColorValue = 255)
gdalraster::plot_raster(r, col_map_fn = temps, legend = TRUE,
                        main = "2 m temperature (K), 2020-01-01 00:00 UTC")
```

![Global 2 m air temperature from ERA5 at midnight UTC on 1 January
2020: coldest over Antarctica, Siberia and Greenland, hottest over
summer Australia](reference/figures/README-global-1.png)

``` r
dbDisconnect(con)
```

## Learn more

[Get started](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/articles/xrdbi.html)
works through connections, statements, parameters, dplyr and rasters on
a small bundled file. Then:

- Querying: [Querying with
  dplyr](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/articles/dplyr.html) (how each
  verb compiles, and what gets read),
  [Parameters](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/articles/parameters.html)
  (R values into statements by name), [From arrays to
  rows](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/articles/rendering.html) (the
  shape and types of results, and when work happens) and [Data
  sources](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/articles/data-sources.html)
  (netCDF over HTTPS, many files, zarr on Google Cloud and S3, GDAL
  rasters and VRTs, icechunk)
- Grids and geometry:
  [Rasters](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/articles/rasters.html),
  [Chunk
  maps](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/articles/chunk-maps.html) and
  [Curvilinear grids and vector
  cubes](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/articles/curvilinear.html)
- [Python
  environments](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/articles/python-environments.html)
  and the [Design
  notes](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/articles/design.html)

In R,
[`?xrdbi`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/xrdbi-package.md)
is the overview: how xarray maps to DBI, the functions by task, and the
options.

## Related

- [DBI for
  xarray](https://github.com/mdsumner/gdal-r-python/blob/main/dbi-xarray/dbi-for-xarray.md),
  the design note, which also sketches the chunk-level relation of an
  array store: chunk keys, byte ranges and encoded blobs
- [storecard](https://github.com/hypertidy/storecard), metadata-only
  descriptions of array stores
- [*Regular in what?*](https://hypertidy.github.io/regular-in-what/), on
  grids, frames and the curvilinear confusion

# Package index

## Overview

- [`xrdbi`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/xrdbi-package.md)
  [`xrdbi-package`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/xrdbi-package.md)
  : xrdbi: 'DBI' Backend for 'xarray' via a Live 'reticulate' Session

Open a connection to an xarray Dataset and look around it.

## Query

Python statements, compiled selections, dplyr verbs, and whole
variables.

- [`dbSendQuery(`*`<XarrayConnection>`*`,`*`<character>`*`)`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/XarrayResult-class.md)
  [`dbBind(`*`<XarrayResult>`*`)`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/XarrayResult-class.md)
  [`show(`*`<XarrayResult>`*`)`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/XarrayResult-class.md)
  [`dbIsValid(`*`<XarrayResult>`*`)`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/XarrayResult-class.md)
  [`dbGetStatement(`*`<XarrayResult>`*`)`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/XarrayResult-class.md)
  [`dbFetch(`*`<XarrayResult>`*`)`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/XarrayResult-class.md)
  [`dbHasCompleted(`*`<XarrayResult>`*`)`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/XarrayResult-class.md)
  [`dbGetRowCount(`*`<XarrayResult>`*`)`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/XarrayResult-class.md)
  [`dbClearResult(`*`<XarrayResult>`*`)`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/XarrayResult-class.md)
  : Xarray result
- [`xr_query()`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/xr_query.md)
  : Compile a structured selection to a Python expression
- [`tbl(`*`<XarrayConnection>`*`)`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/tbl_xarray.md)
  : A lazy dplyr table over an xarray variable
- [`dbReadTable(`*`<XarrayConnection>`*`,`*`<character>`*`)`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/dbReadTable-XarrayConnection-character-method.md)
  : Read a variable as a tidy data frame

## Render other ways

A slab as an in-memory raster, and the storage chunks under a selection.

- [`xr_raster()`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/xr_raster.md)
  : Render a result in gdalraster's in-memory raster format
- [`xr_chunks()`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/xr_chunks.md)
  : Map the chunks a selection touches

## Python objects

- [`xr_dataset()`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/xr_dataset.md)
  [`xr_module()`](https://mdsumner.github.io/xrdbi/reference/xr_dataset.md)
  : Drop to the underlying Python objects
